transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’ve been having these episodes after my evening class. I’ll stop and get a whole fast-food meal, buy candy from the vending machine, then go home and keep eating snacks. It feels like I’m trying to make up for the whole day all at once.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to counteract the food, such as making yourself throw up?
A few times, after those late-night eating spells, I’ve gone to the bathroom and made myself throw up. I was scared all that food would show on me.
Could you tell me your current height and approximately how much you weigh?
I’m not sure of the exact numbers. I haven’t checked my height or weight recently.
On average, how many times a week do you make yourself throw up?
Usually about once a week. It’s been like that for around three months—one night after class where I overeat and then make myself throw up.
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you are eating?
Yeah. Once I start snacking, I keep telling myself to stop, close the bag, and go to bed, but I just keep reaching for more. It feels like I can’t make myself stop until I feel sick and embarrassed.
How much does your body weight or shape influence how you feel about yourself as a person?

Quite a bit, honestly. If my shirt feels tight around my middle, I feel like I’ve failed somehow—like I’m not being the careful, disciplined person I’m supposed to be. Even if everything else, like my bookkeeping work, is going fine.
Have you recently experienced significant weight loss, or has a doctor ever told you that you are underweight?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any major weight loss, and no doctor has told me I’m underweight.
Have you ever had a time in the past where you severely restricted your eating and became very underweight?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve never had a period where I was severely restricting food or got very underweight.
